problem_meta.agent_answer:
Plan:
1. [✓] Analyzed the sequence against reviewed protein annotations.
2. [✓] Identified the homolog-supported catalytic reaction and cofactor.

## Functional summary

The 509-amino-acid protein is most likely a **UDP-N-acetylmuramoyl-L-alanyl-D-glutamate—meso-2,6-diaminopimelate ligase (MurE; EC 6.3.2.13)**. Its closest reviewed matches are cyanobacterial proteins, with **about 40–42% sequence identity across nearly the full length**.

The enzyme is predicted to add **meso-diaminopimelate (meso-DAP)** to the D-glutamate residue of the peptidoglycan precursor UDP-MurNAc-L-Ala-D-Glu. This extends the peptide stem used to build bacterial cell-wall peptidoglycan.

**Reaction:**

> UDP-N-acetyl-α-D-muramoyl-L-alanyl-D-glutamate + meso-2,6-diaminopimelate + ATP  
> → UDP-N-acetyl-α-D-muramoyl-L-alanyl-γ-D-glutamyl-meso-2,6-diaminopimelate + ADP + phosphate + H⁺

The homolog annotations indicate **Mg²⁺** dependence.

**Evidence caveat:** The function and reaction are supported by strong, full-length homology to reviewed proteins, not by a direct activity measurement of this particular sequence. The tool report therefore grades the functional assignment as moderate homology support.
